rows.subtype: Team hit by a late finisher [Receiver]
rows.description: A colleague waiting for someone else's late input has to compress their own work and stay late to compensate. Missed deadlines rarely fall only on the person who missed them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Warning early when a deadline will slip [Response]
rows.description: A responsible worker tells others as soon as a date looks unsafe, with a new realistic date and options. Early bad news can be planned around; late bad news is felt as a betrayal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Exams, tuition, family and friends together [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager juggles school, coaching classes, family events and friends and feels pulled apart, snapping at people close by. The overload shows first as irritability, not as a clear complaint.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student joins every club, helps every friend and takes every offer, then falls behind on the core work. Fear of disappointing others and fear of missing out both push toward overcommitment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A peer notices someone missing details, sighing often and skipping lunch, all signs of too many demands. A useful gesture is asking what could be taken off their plate, not adding advice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Work, family and personal duties colliding [Actor]
rows.description: A young professional balances a demanding job, parents' expectations and personal life, feeling guilty about whichever is neglected. Duty and resentment often sit together and neither cancels the other.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A spouse or parent notices that a person constantly busy with work is present in body but distracted, and feels quietly last on the list. The effect is often unspoken until it becomes a big argument.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A wise person lists all commitments, tells relevant people what will be delayed, and does one thing at a time. Being honest about limits is less harmful than silently failing at several things.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Child too shy or proud to ask [Actor]
rows.description: A schoolchild sits confused over a problem and says nothing, afraid of looking stupid in front of classmates. Silence feels safer than exposure, so confusion quietly grows.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, shyness, confusion, pride

rows.description: A teenager struggles alone with a subject because asking a teacher feels like admitting failure, especially among peers who seem to understand. Pride and fear of judgment cost weeks of avoidable struggle.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
